summary: Module 4 DECIDE. Decision 1 (decisions.module_04.profiling_strategy): B -- Manual profiling with the runtime's free built-ins (cProfile + py-spy for CPU, tracemalloc for memory). Reasoning: zero vendor cost, no per-request agent overhead, no lock-in, and I control exactly what is measured. For a single-service lab APM pays off around ~5+ engineers with a running incident rotation; at this size the dashboards are more ceremony than signal. Risk of profiling production is real (sampler overhead on hot paths, transient CPU spikes, and heap snapshots doubling apparent RSS), so for a live prod service I would only attach py-spy briefly on a low-traffic window or a canary -- for this lab the API is effectively the canary. If I could only afford one I pick CPU first for a general slowdown investigation, because a service that is slow is usually waiting (CPU or I/O); I would miss memory leaks, so I would pair the CPU hot-spot finding with a tracemalloc/top snapshot before declaring done. Decision 2 (decisions.module_04.inspection_scope): A then B -- start broad (attach sampler, run the general load test, get the heat map) and use the broad results to form a hypothesis, then narrow the profiler onto the single hot endpoint. When I have no idea what is wrong: broad. When a specific user reports one slow endpoint: targeted immediately. The combine-the-two answer is the funnel: broad scan to find the anomaly, targeted profile to confirm and drill into it.
